content: BTW if you open that Markdown file in BonBon you get the rendering not the source. I have to get used to that, there are two webs, one for Markdown and one for HTML. I think some people are offering Markdown versions of HTML files. We're going to this too, and have a website that'll be a perfect test case -- this.how. What's good about it is that it is a rendering of OPML files, so we don't have to work with the HTML at all, we can and will create and OPML to Markdown converter. And then when we want to put it on a domain for BonBon's use, just add ?format=markdown to the URL. It doesn't work yet but it will.
